content.text: {"utterance":"Leonie, rebuilding from the idea is neither plain recall nor proof of use. If the changed problem is just the same proof with different letters, it's a disguised repeat. It counts for me when the same idea has to be bent: say the original needed a positive number and now zero is allowed, so they must find which step breaks and repair it. Like the risotto cook whose rice absorbs liquid differently. Your point also costs me something: adaptation depends on recalled structure, so recall isn't separate from use. What I'd withhold is \"learned the proof\" from the reciter, though \"learned the sequence\" fits.","cites":["NI3"],"memory":"Claim: learning is adapting in a situation where a step must be repaired, not just relabeled; concede adaptation depends on recalled structure. Reciter learned sequence, not proof. Live question: can a lucky repair or practiced pattern still pass as new?"}
